sources.title: MetMalaysia — Weather phenomena
sources.claim: Northeast Monsoon Nov–Mar brings heavy rain to east coast peninsula, west Sarawak and east Sabah; Southwest Monsoon late May–Sep is drier; inter-monsoon Apr–May and Oct–Nov.

sources.title: Intrepid Travel — Weather in Malaysia
sources.claim: Northeast Monsoon Nov–Mar hits Perhentian/Redang/Tioman, west Sarawak, east Sabah; lowlands 23–33°C, humidity 80%+ year-round.

sources.title: Backpacking Bella — Perhentian Islands
sources.claim: Perhentians open Mar–Oct, best May–Sep, peak Jun–Aug, effectively closed Nov–Feb.

sources.title: AirTraveler — East-coast monsoon warning
sources.claim: East-coast islands closed Nov–Feb; ferries resume late February; ~25 rain days in November.

sources.title: 4stogo — Monsoon closures & accessibility
sources.claim: Most east-coast island accommodation closes during the monsoon due to bad weather and rough seas.

sources.title: Enchanting Travels — Best time to visit Malaysia
sources.claim: West coast best Dec–Mar; east coast best Apr–Oct; Borneo best Mar–Oct; regions have opposite wet seasons.

sources.title: Weather & Climate — Sandakan
sources.claim: Sandakan (east Sabah) wettest in December (~301mm); Nov–Dec can exceed 400mm.

sources.title: Amazing Borneo — Kinabatangan River
sources.claim: Kinabatangan wettest and often flooded Dec–Jan; peak wildlife activity May–Aug.

sources.title: Responsible Travel — Best time to visit Sabah
sources.claim: Sabah's wet season runs roughly Oct–Mar; the relatively dry May–Sep is best for wildlife and trekking.

sources.title: Climates to Travel — Kuching
sources.claim: Kuching (west Sarawak) wettest Nov–Feb; January is the wettest month at ~670mm.

sources.title: Weather & Climate — Kuching rainfall
sources.claim: Kuching January is the wettest month with ~672mm of precipitation.

sources.title: Responsible Travel — Best time to visit Sarawak
sources.claim: Sarawak is wettest Nov–Feb; the drier Mar–Sep window is the better time to visit.

sources.title: timeanddate — Malaysia holidays 2026
sources.claim: 2026: Chinese New Year 17–18 Feb, Thaipusam 2 Feb, Deepavali 8 Nov.

sources.title: Eskimo Travel — Malaysia public holidays 2026
sources.claim: Ramadan 2026 begins ~20 Feb; Hari Raya Aidilfitri ~21–22 Mar 2026 with a 4-day long weekend and balik-kampung travel surge.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Southeast Asian haze
sources.claim: Transboundary haze from Indonesian peat/forest fires recurs in the Jun–Oct dry season, worst in strong El Niño years (1997, 2015, 2019, 2023).

sources.title: Indoneo — SE Asia El Niño & haze 2026 forecast
sources.claim: 2026 haze risk flagged worst since 2015: El Niño ~80% likely by July, positive IOD in Jul–Aug, peak haze Aug–Sep, echoing 1997.

sources.title: The Star — Haze alarm in Southeast Asia
sources.claim: By late March 2026, rising fire hotspots and scant rain had already raised haze alarm across Southeast Asia.

sources.title: Batam News — Johor peat fire
sources.claim: A Pengerang, Johor peat fire ignited 23 Jan 2026 and grew to ~100 hectares by 27 Jan, forcing evacuations.

sources.title: Rainforest World Music Festival
sources.claim: Rainforest World Music Festival 2026 runs 26–28 June at the Sarawak Cultural Village, Kuching.

sources.title: Odynovo Tours — Best time to visit Malaysia
sources.claim: West coast best Dec–Mar (escapes NE monsoon); Borneo best Mar–Oct, relatively dry May–Oct for parks.

sources.title: Selective Asia — Malaysia weather
sources.claim: When the east coast is wet and windy the west coast is nicer and vice versa, so somewhere has good weather year-round.

sources.title: Intrepid Travel — Best time to visit Malaysia
sources.claim: West coast best Nov–Mar; east coast best Apr–Oct (hotels close late Oct–Mar); Borneo best Mar–Oct.
